commits.summary: Added veroboard
Fixed builds lint issue and removed accidentally committed tutorial work
Added 2 switches that cross the trench 1-push switch DPDT, 2-Tactile 6mm
Add release notes page, updated on every make release
Smoother editing on busy desks: much faster drags, repeated notifications merged, and Space runs the circuit with a wire tool armed.
Added the 74LS92, custom clock rates, and a Timing or Transitions axis for the logic analyzer.
A new selection and drag model, the real 10-pin 7-segment display, bendable TO-92 legs, and rotation for every component.
Fixes from a whole-codebase bug review, and a what's-new banner for people upgrading.
Fixed LEDs on a PWM clock lagging behind a thrown switch (reported by minecon1776).
Spice Lite: amplitude and offset for clock waves, truer 74LS inputs and outputs, and more areas graded against ngspice.
Spice Lite: switch contact bounce, and LEDs that show a PWM signal's average brightness.
Added a speaker that plays the tone across it under Spice Lite, with a 555 example.
Added Spice Lite, a second simulation engine that works in voltages and currents: real LEDs, chip limits and brown smoke.
Spice Lite graded against ngspice: exact RC and inductor networks, datasheet diode and LED curves, and transistor grades.
Transistor part numbers with preset figures, the split power-rail strip, and better value fields.
Updated the user guide and its PDF.
Spice Lite: CMOS outputs follow their datasheet's current curve.
Spice Lite fixes for inductors, RC timing and the CD4000 timers.
Updated the user guide and its PDF.
Added the bench parts (LM358, ULN2003A, optocouplers, voltage regulators, relay, electronic load) and triangle, sawtooth and sine clock waves.
Spice Lite runs several times faster.
Clocks can be a PWM signal with a set pulse width, or a trapezoid wave under Spice Lite.
500 Hz and 1 kHz clocks are back, with fixes to the memory inspector, the updater, paste and the schematic.
Added the CPU monitor for the W65C02 and Z80A, and "Hello World" example computers for both.
CPU monitor: breakpoints saved with the project, and CPU core fixes.
CPU monitor: Pause, Step Over, Go to, the stack, a breakpoint list and editable registers.
Release checks: RC and LC example circuits, and fixes to the updater, project tabs and CPU monitor.
Release checks: updater and simulation fixes.
Release checks: fixes to chip seating, ROM loading, the 3D view and opening projects.
Website: new hero shots for the latest features.
Updated the user guide, including auto-routing every wire.
Website: names the CD4000 CMOS family beside 74xx.
Added the 3D view of the desk.
Wide (600-mil) chips seat at their real width.
Added the custom chip designer: describe a chip in Verilog, place it, and debug it while the circuit runs.
Website: three new hero shots and feature cards.
More Verilog for custom chips: inout ports, memories, loops and signed arithmetic.
Pre-release fixes to the chip designer, its debugger and project tabs.
Updated the user guide PDF.
Added the CD4000 CMOS family, the 555 timer and a potentiometer.
Added capacitors, diodes, inductors and transistors.
Typed component values with pick lists, three more CD4000 parts, and a datasheet review of the whole family.
Renamed the CD4511B's pin 5 to LE/STROBE, as its datasheet does.
Relicensed from Apache-2.0 to GPL-3.0-or-later, with an exception that keeps generated board code free to use.
Updated the App Store listing for Serial I/O, auto-routing and the GPL.
Website: linked the new supported-chips page.
Website: added the supported-chips page, generated from the parts catalog.
Documented the serial-port entitlement for App Store review.
Added export to a KiCad schematic and to Digital (.dig).
Fixes from a whole-project review: the 74LS181's functions, closing the window, corrupt projects, Z80 interrupts and undo during drags.
Moved the CI actions to Node 24.
Fixed the Linux build.
Fixed the Mac App Store build.
A better schematic view layout, with zoom.
Added auto-routing: redraw every wire as a board-aligned run around the parts.
Added external signals: on-screen inputs you plant on the board with a flag.
Build fixes.
Fixed a dragged wire end landing on a hole out of reach.
Several external signals, each with its own id.
The desk's scroll lock is saved in the project file.
Added icons to the component tray.
Tray icons match the app icon's colour.
Added a setting to auto-close component tray folders.
Auto-routing asks before it starts.
Each clock can be paused and resumed on its own.
Added Serial I/O: a running circuit talks to a real Arduino-class board over USB. The AI builder was hardened too.
Serial I/O: reworked viewing and saving the generated board code.
Serial I/O: the wire protocol documented in the user guide, with conformance tests.
Updated the example serial sketch.
Serial I/O review fixes; each platform's build ships only its own serial-port binaries.
Website: updated the feature list.
Release builds upload to the Mac App Store automatically.
Website: added the Mac App Store link.
LED bulbs are drawn centred on their legs.
R turns a breadboard strip while you place it.
Resistor arrays can be turned end for end.
DIP switches show their ON label.
Code quality: the desk controller split into smaller pieces.
Wire waypoints are hidden while the circuit runs.
Submitted to the Mac App Store.
Website: "Other Hippos" became "Visit the hippo herd".
Fixed a website test that broke the build.
Updated the README.
Updated the README.
Updated the roadmap.
Addressed the Mac App Store review's concerns.
Website: added a feature request link.
Website: added a feedback link to the navigation bar.
Release and App Store publishing notes for 1.0.1.
Prepared the Mac App Store build: sandbox-safe file access and the publishing checklist.
Added the 65xx example computers, with their ROM images.
Added the Z80A CPU and reorganised the processor parts.
Website: updated the hero breadboard.
The Properties dialog lists a chip's live warnings.
Added AI desk review: ask the AI to check a circuit you built by hand.
Website: refreshed the hero breadboard.
AI-built circuits use both power rails, short power wires and a single rail-to-rail link.
Website: the hero shows several breadboards.
Project files carry memory chip contents, so one file holds the whole design.
Cmd/Ctrl-click adds a part or wire to the selection, or takes it out.
Clocks can run at 100 Hz.
A multi-part selection drags as one unit.
Updated the user guide and keyboard shortcuts.
Code review fixes for the website's downloads, version history and release signing.
